label: Accolade attribute level
summary: Whether one attribute of the accolade is at a given level.
details: Runs on an accolade. You name the attribute type and compare its level with `level`, using <, <=, =, !=, > or >=.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which accolade attribute to look at.
fields.values: an accolade attribute type, such as bruiser_accolade

label: Can get more attributes
summary: Whether the accolade can still take more attributes, because it has not reached the maximum number.
details: Runs on an accolade. Write `yes` for "can still get more" or `no` for "is full".

label: Has unspent attribute
summary: Whether the accolade has attributes that are not yet spent.
details: Runs on an accolade. Vanilla only uses it with `yes`.

label: Accolade rank
summary: Compares the rank of the accolade with a number.
details: Runs on an accolade. Vanilla mostly compares with >= or <, for example `accolade_rank >= 5`.

label: Accolade type tier
summary: Whether the tier of the accolade type is equal to a given value.
details: Runs on an accolade type. The game gives no usage line and vanilla does not use it, so the exact value format is not shown.

label: De jure drift progress
summary: Compares the active de jure drift progress of a title with a number.
details: Runs on a title. The game's documentation is only an example line, `task_current_value = scope:county.active_de_jure_drift_progress`, and vanilla does not use it, so what exactly the number means and its unit are not stated.

label: Add to temporary list
summary: Saves a temporary target under a list name while the trigger runs, to build a list inside a trigger.
details: It sits among the triggers but is used to build lists, not to test anything. Inside an `any_` trigger the game stops at the first match, so to collect every match use `count = all` and put this at the very end of the `any_` trigger. Vanilla gives it just a list name, for example `murder_targets`.

fields.name: list name
fields.text: The name of the temporary list to add to.

label: Age
summary: Compares the character's age with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla mostly writes plain comparisons like `age >= 12`. It also writes a range `{ 16 25 }` and a block with `value = root.age` and `subtract = ...`; the game's documentation does not explain those two forms.

label: Agent contribution
summary: Compares the contribution value given by a filled agent slot with a number.
details: Runs on an agent slot that is filled. Compare with <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Agent gives contribution type
summary: Whether the agent slot provides a given type of contribution.
details: Runs on an agent slot. Written as `agent_slot_has_contribution_type = <type>`, where the type is one of secrecy, success_chance, success_chance_growth, success_chance_max or speed. Vanilla uses it once, with `secrecy`.

label: AI boldness
summary: Compares the character's AI boldness value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0, plain numbers like 25 or 50 and named constants like `medium_positive_ai_value`.

label: AI compassion
summary: Compares the character's AI compassion value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0 and with named constants like `low_positive_ai_value`.

label: AI diplomatic stance
summary: Whether the AI character's diplomatic view of a given other character is neutral, a threat, an enemy or a friend.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it with `target = root` and the stance `friend` or `neutral`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character the AI is judging.

label: AI energy
summary: Compares the character's AI energy value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares with 0, plain numbers and named constants like `low_positive_ai_value`.

label: AI greed
summary: Compares the character's AI greed value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0, plain numbers up to 100 and named constants like `medium_positive_ai_value`.

label: AI honor
summary: Compares the character's AI honor value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0, plain numbers and named constants like `high_positive_ai_value`.

label: AI rationality
summary: Compares the character's AI rationality value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0 and with negative numbers like -25 and -50, as well as named constants.

label: AI sociability
summary: Compares the character's AI sociability value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0, plain numbers from -75 to 100 and named constants.

label: AI values divergence
summary: Compares how different the AI values of the character and another character are, added up over all values.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla writes it as a block with `target` and a comparison such as `value >= high_ai_values_divergence`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character to compare with.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the summed difference.

label: AI vengefulness
summary: Compares the character's AI vengefulness value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0, plain numbers and named constants.

label: AI will do contribution
summary: Compares how willing the character is, at base, to make a given contribution.
details: Runs on a character. The documented example is `scope:my_char.contribution_ai_will_do( scope:great_project_contribution ) > 25`, so the contribution is given in that parenthesis form. The input shows no vanilla use of this key.

label: AI zeal
summary: Compares the character's AI zeal value with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0, plain numbers up to 100 and named constants.

label: Court artifact slots
summary: Whether all of the character's court artifact slots are empty or all are full.
details: Runs on a character. The game's documentation does not say how to choose between empty and full, and vanilla does not use it, so the value format is not shown.

label: All false (NOR)
summary: Whether every trigger inside it is false.
details: Works the same as NOR. It passes only when none of the conditions inside pass.

label: Inventory artifact slots
summary: Whether all of the character's inventory artifact slots are empty or all are full.
details: Runs on a character. The game's documentation does not say how to choose between empty and full, and vanilla does not use it, so the value format is not shown.

label: Early retreat allowed
summary: Whether this side of a battle may retreat early when it is losing.
details: Runs on a combat side. The flag is set with the effect `set_allow_early_retreat = yes`. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Can have concubines
summary: Whether the character is allowed to have concubines.
details: Runs on a character. The game's documentation asks whether they can have concubines, which reads as permission rather than whether they have any now. Vanilla only uses `yes`.

label: Can have more concubines
summary: Whether the character may have more concubines.
details: Runs on a character. The documented wording ("more") suggests it differs from `allowed_concubines` by also looking at how many they already have. Vanilla only uses `yes`.

label: Can have more spouses
summary: Whether the character may have more spouses.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla only uses `yes`.

label: Always
summary: A condition that is simply true (`yes`) or false (`no`), or follows a yes/no value saved earlier.
details: `always = yes` always passes and `always = no` never passes. You can also give a saved yes/no value such as `scope:hook`, which is looked up when the script runs. Vanilla uses it mostly as a fixed yes or no.

label: Amenity level
summary: Compares the character's court amenity level in a given type (food, lodging, fashion or servants as vanilla uses it) with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses the block form with `target` as the amenity type (court_food_quality, court_lodging_standards, court_fashion or court_servants). The short form `amenity_level:court_lodging_standards > 1` also exists in the game's documentation.

fields.name: target
fields.values: court_food_quality, court_lodging_standards, court_fashion or court_servants (as used by vanilla)

fields.name: value
fields.values: a comparison such as `value >= 5`, or a named level like `medium_amenity_level`

label: And
summary: Whether all triggers inside it are true.
details: Vanilla uses it once, to group `ai_greed >= 100` and `ai_honor < 0`.

label: Appointment accumulated score
summary: Compares a character's accumulated score as a candidate for appointment to a given title.
details: Runs on a character. Only investment counts here, not the character's personality. Written as a block with `target` (the title) and `value`, or in the form `"appointment_candidate_accumulated_score(scope:title)" >= value`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The title the character is a candidate for.

label: Appointment total score
summary: Compares a character's total score as a candidate for appointment to a given title.
details: Runs on a character. Written as a block with `target` and `value`, or as `"appointment_candidate_score(scope:title)" >= value`. The game's documentation calls this the total score, and the accumulated-score trigger counts investment only.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The title the character is a candidate for.

label: Appointment level for title
summary: Compares the currency level the character needs for an appointment to a given title.
details: Runs on a character. Written as a block with `target` (the title) and `value`, or in the form `scope:character.appointment_level_for_title(scope:target_title) > 2`.

label: Days until appointment
summary: Compares how many days until the character can take part in an appointment.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla compares it with 0 and with day counts such as 365.

label: Court position aptitude
summary: Compares the character's aptitude in a given court position type with a number.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla always uses the block form, mostly with `value >= 3` or `>= 4`.

fields.name: court_position
fields.text: The court position type to rate the character for.
fields.values: a court position type, such as master_of_hunt_court_position

label: Is moving
summary: Whether the army is moving.
details: Runs on an army. Write `yes` for moving or `no` for not moving.

label: Army max size
summary: Compares the maximum size of the army with a number.
details: Runs on an army. Vanilla does not use it, so no typical values are shown.

label: Number of MaA regiments
summary: Compares how many men-at-arms (MaA) regiments the army has with a number.
details: Runs on an army. Vanilla does not use it.
